what_this_is: The Workshop rows for sending a message from the person's AI: an email, a text or a Messages message on the person's own Mac, to one person or a list, and turning a document into a message body first. A tool is named for its job, never for a vendor: the request names the provider (an id from read-data/message-providers.json, the one the person's connection of that role is), and the row mounts only that provider's keys (each credential item carries only_when, the engine's input-named mount), so a new provider is one entry in read-data/message-providers.json and its mounts here, never a new tool. The person's own key reaches the one process on private pipes and is never in the request. Two rows pace a sending inbox and sort what comes back (bounces, complaints, replies) by the pacing and outcome rows of read-data/inbox-pacing.json.

payload.label: Send an email
payload.job: Send an email, to one person or a list, through the email provider I connected
payload.description: Give recipients (a list of addresses; to for one), provider (the id of the email provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's email connection is), the settings that provider's row asks for (region for Amazon SES, such as us-east-1) and the words: subject and text (drawn as an email in the look the person wears, in the person's saved screen look, which the caller hands in as `saved` (the shipped look until they choose one; an email whose look cannot be read is not sent), with its mark from the mail row's site and made_with) or your own html, markdown for a written email (it also goes as a BCC to the account's own address, and answers sent_copy), or template (a template name from read-data/message-templates.json, or your own templates) with variables; kind names what it is for the account's limits (sign-in-code, message ...). Every email comes from the account's own mail row, which the caller hands in as mail_settings (read from the person's `mail-settings` row `settings:mail`; with none the shipped row names no sender and nothing is sent), never from the request; each address may be sent only so many emails of a kind (per_person, counted from the mail_sent rows handed in), the day keeps room for sign-in codes (daily, counted from the mail_day row handed in), a proof address is never sent, and every email is written down under its address: nothing is kept here, the answer's keep holds the mail-sent and mail-day rows as the send left them, each with the row it expected, for the caller to write. Each recipient is sent to on their own and answered on their own: sent holds { recipient, messageId } or { recipient, error } with limited, unknown (it may have gone; it is not sent again) or suppressed. The held keys of the provider named reach the one process on private pipes; they are never shown.

mail_settings.description: The account's mail row (its `settings:mail` row of kind mail-settings: the sender, limits, proof names and site), read from the person's store; left out, the shipped row, which names no sender, so nothing is sent

mail_sent.description: The person's `mail-sent` rows ({ id, type, value }) the limits count, read from their store

mail_day.description: The day's `mail-day` row ({ id, type, value }), read from the person's store

saved.description: The person's saved look values by name, read by the caller from where the person keeps them and handed in (the engine keeps none): screen-look, screen-look-own-themes, workspace-preference:screen-look-over-time and workspace-preference:where-looks-apply, each with its value. What is not given is not there.

value.description: The row to keep; null removes it

expected.description: The row as it was handed in ({ type, value }), or null when it was absent; write it with this as the condition

keep.description: The rows this run changed, as they should be kept: the run keeps nothing itself

provenance.source: bitfield-packages broadcast-delivery (Amazon SES adapter) and resend-email-sender (templates, headers), ported

payload.label: Send a text message
payload.job: Send a text message, to one number or a list, through the text provider I connected
payload.description: Give recipients (phone numbers with country code; to for one), provider (the id of the text provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's text connection is), the settings that row asks for (for twilio-sms: from, a number on the account, and account_sid, the account's id) and text (or subject when there is no text). Each number is sent to on its own and answered on its own: sent holds { recipient, messageId }, { recipient, error, unknown: false } when the provider confirmed a rejection before the message was made, or { recipient, error, unknown: true } when it may have gone and must not be retried blindly. The held key of the provider named reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown.

payload.label: Send a message in Messages on this Mac
payload.job: Send a message to one person or a list from the Messages app on the person's own Mac
payload.description: Give recipients (phone numbers or Apple ids Messages knows; to for one) and text. Each recipient is sent to on their own and answered on their own: sent holds { recipient } or { recipient, error }. The text goes to Messages as its own argument, never inside the script. If the Mac has not allowed this to control Messages, nothing is sent and the answer says what to allow in System Settings, Privacy and Security, Automation.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages imessage-messages-sender (the Messages script as DATA, permission classification), ported

payload.label: Turn a document into a message body (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn a document I wrote (headings, paragraphs, images, a quoted reply) into the HTML and plain-text body of a message, ready to send
payload.description: Takes a request file { document_nodes: [{ id, kind, props, children, visible }] or one root node, options? } and writes { body_html, body_text, inline_refs, degraded }. Text and heading kinds become paragraphs and headings with a plain-text line each; image and media blocks become inline_refs { cid, fetch_ref, mime } for the sender to attach; blocks marked as a quote become one blockquote with > lines; hidden subtrees are skipped; a block kind it does not know falls back to its text and is listed in degraded, never dropped silently. options.kind_renderers maps your own block kinds to paragraph, heading1 to heading3 or media. It names no mail provider.

request.description: Path of the request JSON file

output.description: Path to write the result JSON to

output_schema.description: Exit 0 and one summary line: the HTML and text sizes, the number of parts and of degraded blocks. The output file holds { body_html, body_text, inline_refs, degraded }.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request file from the document, run `run`, then read the output file. Hand body_html and body_text to the sending tool as html and text. Tell the person about every entry in degraded (a block that could not be shown as itself). If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

payload.label: Sign someone up for an email course
payload.job: Sign a person up for an email course after they agreed to it, keep their consent in my records, send the first lesson now and queue the others
payload.description: Give email, consent (true only when the person agreed in the words of course.consent_text), course (id, public_origin as an https site root, checkout_url, from, mailing_address, consent_text, consent_version and 2 to 12 lessons { delay_hours, subject, article_url, text_lines, html_lines } where every lesson carries {{unsubscribeUrl}} and {{mailingAddress}} and the first has delay_hours 0), source (where they signed up, optional) records (the person's rows listed in its schema, read from their store) and provider (the id of the email provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's email connection is; region too when that row asks for one). Nothing is sent without consent, a sender and a mailing address. Works out the consent row with its words, version, time and source and each later lesson's queue row at its time (tool:send-due-email-lessons sends them), and answers them in keep for the caller to write; nothing is kept here; sends lesson 1 with List-Unsubscribe headers; signing up again sends nothing twice. Answers { status: enrolled, already_enrolled }.

payload.label: Send the email lessons that have come due
payload.job: Send each email-course lesson whose time has come to the people still signed up, once each, and retry a failed one later
payload.description: Give records (the person's queue, subscription, token and contact rows, read from their store), optional limit (up to 50 per run), provider (the id of the email provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's email connection is) and region when that row asks for one. Finds the queued lessons whose time has passed, sends each to a subscriber who is still signed up and has not had it, works out the subscription's sent mark and the queue entry's removal, and answers them in keep for the caller to write. A failed send queues its own retry (up to three, each later than the last). Answers results [{ lesson_index, status: sent, already-sent, unsubscribed or failed, why? }] and said.

payload.label: Who agreed to get which emails
payload.job: Show who agreed to get which email list, in what words, when and from where, and whether they still do

payload.label: Pace sends from an inbox
payload.job: Say when each address on a list may be emailed from one sending inbox, so a new inbox warms up slowly, sends only on chosen days and hours, and stops when its mail bounces
payload.description: Give time_zone (the inbox's), recipients and a pacing row (pacing: new-inbox-warmup or saturday-local from read-data/inbox-pacing.json, or your own pacing_row): a ramp of sends a day by the inbox's day number, the least gap between sends, weekdays, local hours, how many days to leave an address after it was sent to, and when to pause (a share of hard bounces or any complaint among the last sends). Add history (every send this inbox made), outcomes (from tool:sort-bounces-and-replies) and suppressed addresses. Returns due_now (send these now, through a send tool), schedule (a slot for every address that may be sent to, in local time with its ramp day), held (each address left out and why: suppressed, bounced, unsubscribed, replied, sent to recently, listed twice, not an address, or the inbox is paused) and paused. It sends nothing and keeps nothing; every number, day and hour is a row you can change.

pacing.description: A pacing row id from read-data/inbox-pacing.json: new-inbox-warmup or saturday-local.

pacing_row.description: Your own pacing row: { id, ramp: [{ from_day, per_day }], min_gap_minutes, weekdays, hours: { from, to }, leave_address_days, pause_when: { last_sends, bounce_share_at_least, complaints_at_least } }.

time_zone.description: The sending inbox's IANA time zone; weekdays and hours are read in it.

first_send_at.description: When this inbox first sent; its local day is day 1 of the ramp. Defaults to its earliest send in history, else the first send planned now.

provenance.source: outreach methods that send from a separate, warmed-up inbox at a set pace and stop on bounces and replies, generalised into pacing and outcome rows

payload.label: Sort bounces and replies
payload.job: Sort the bounces, complaints, unsubscribes and replies that came back from emails I sent, and say which addresses never to send to again, which to retry and which people wrote back
payload.description: Give events as your provider or mailbox gave them and event_source (plain, resend-webhook, amazon-ses-notification or mailbox-message from read-data/inbox-pacing.json, or your own event_source_row naming where the recipient, type, status, subject, text and time sit). Each event is read into those fields and the first outcome row whose every condition holds (a field equals one of its values, contains one of its words, or matches its pattern) names its kind (hard-bounce, soft-bounce, complaint, unsubscribe, reply, auto-reply, delivered) and action (suppress, stop-sequence, retry-later, hand-to-person, none). Returns outcomes (hand them to tool:pace-sends-from-an-inbox), suppress, stop, retry (with when), replies and the unmatched events. It sends, deletes and keeps nothing; your own outcome_rows replace the shipped ones.

events.description: The bounces, complaints, delivery notices and replies that came back, as the provider or mailbox gave them.

event_source.description: An event-source row id from read-data/inbox-pacing.json: plain (default), resend-webhook, amazon-ses-notification or mailbox-message.

event_source_row.description: Your own event-source row: { id, fields: { recipient, type, status?, subject?, text?, at? } }, each a dot path into an event.

outcome_rows.description: Your own outcome rows in order: { id, when: [{ field, equals | matching | pattern }], kind, action, retry_after_hours?, says? }. The first whose every condition holds wins.

provenance.source: outreach methods that send from a separate, warmed-up inbox at a set pace and stop on bounces and replies, generalised into pacing and outcome rows
